keep: The idea is named up front: a capacitor fills near each peak, feeds the load between them, and in a drive it is the store of DC.

The picture is the brief's reservoir: the bridge feeding a capacitor and a load, sliders for capacitance and load current, the bus riding the humps with its gulps, a ripple readout computed from I ÷ (f × C), and Switch on with precharge off (a red 325 A spike) and on (the charging curve, the contactor after five time constants).

The ripple rule is derived on screen from i = C dv/dt, a rule Dan already has, and its error is stated honestly: it takes the fall to last the whole period, so the drawn dip (about 18 V) sits a little under the readout (20 V).

Both brief misconceptions get a DO screen with their own hints: 'the capacitor adds voltage' (screen 2, the no-load bus) and 'only C sets ripple' (screen 6, the notes' own check, double the load). Screen 12 turns the rule round to size a capacitor.
The 566 V and 540 V are both taught, each with its condition (screen 8), the 1.35 cited and the 566 V computed.
The Exponentials recall sits where it is used (screen 10: five time constants, 'Still there').

fix: Causal step skipped (gulps): screen 3 and explain say the supply's current comes in short, tall gulps but not why. Say all the charge drained over 10 ms goes back in a short refill, so each gulp runs at several times the load current.

Causal step skipped (inrush): screen 9 jumps from 'voltage rises only as fast as current fills it' to 'short circuit'. Say that at the first instant it still holds 0 V while current pours in, which is what a short circuit does, so the whole peak falls across the 1 Ω. Also say why the spike dies within about 5 ms: five time constants of 1 Ω × 1000 µF.
Causal step skipped (screen 1): 'the hump falls away faster than the capacitor' needs its reason, the capacitor drains only slowly through the load.

False absolute: 'It fills only from the supply, so it cannot go higher' (screen 2's Why and explain). A real supply's inductance can nudge a lightly loaded capacitor past the peak at switch-on. Say it settles at the peak and adds no voltage of its own.
Brief shows the effect without the cause: name the slope between peaks getting twice as steep, which is the cause of the deeper dip.

Answer given away: screen 7's Read and still show 400 V three-phase at 5 A with the ripple at 17 V, which is screen 13's answer. End screen 7 on 230 V at 4 A and keep the three-phase link in the words only.
Unreadable label: the readout 'Bus average' and the Read say 'bus', but screen 1 never names the bus. Name the capacitor's voltage as the DC bus in screen 1 and in explain.

Quantity idea without the shape of the rule: add a small plot of ripple against load current for the capacitance set, a straight line through zero with a dot at the setting, so doubling shows as a line.
Assumed values must read as chosen: 'With 1 Ω of supply and wiring' and 'Through 100 Ω' in explain become 'say' values.
Practice: one bullet runs to 25 words; split it. 'It keeps its charge after isolation' becomes 'It can keep its charge', since bleed resistors drain it in time.
